messages:
sarah.j: Quick sync — I'm starting a small RFC for tenant log access. Need input on RBAC rules for audit logs, schema fields we should expose to customers, and how scoped tokens affect visibility. TL;DR: who sees what? 😬

mike.t: +1. We should separate "who can read audit logs" vs "who can see tenant identifiers inside events". Admins should get full event, members only masked tenant_id unless explicitly allowed.

jena: Agree. Also need to decide if customer-facing events mirror internal events or are a filtered projection. I prefer filtered projection with an explicit mapping table.

rafael: Question: do we attach KMS-encrypted blobs for sensitive fields (e.g., email, user ip) or store redacted fields and put full payload behind encrypted archival? KMS integration will add complexity but good for compliance.

priya.k: For HIPAA-ish customers we'd need encrypted PII at rest + strict key access. My suggestion: keep a customer-visible stream that is redacted, and a customer-only encrypted archive with access via scoped token + audit access policy.

sarah.j: Good points. For schema, proposal:
```
{
  "event_id": "uuid",
  "timestamp": "rfc3339",
  "actor": {"id": "string", "role": "string"},
  "action": "string",
  "resource": "string",
  "tenant_id": "string",  // maybe redacted in member view
  "metadata": { ... },
  "sensitivity": "low|medium|high",
  "archived_encrypted_blob": "s3://..." // optional
}
```
We add `sensitivity` to drive redaction and retention policies.

mike.t: Love `sensitivity`. A few follow-ups: who sets it? runtime (service) or ingestion pipeline? We should default to `medium` for anything with user identifiers. Also need a validation step on ingestion to ensure tenant_id aligns with request scope.

jena: On validation: we should have a unit test harness that replays sample actions and asserts the customer-facing projection contains only allowed fields. Add an integration test that exchanges a scoped token and queries events.

rafael: Scoped tokens: implement a scoped JWT with claims `scope: audit:read:tenant:{tenant_id}` and role claims. Token introspection endpoint returns allowed `fields` array so UI can hide fields client-side.

priya.k: Also add policy for cross-tenant admins: e.g., `platform:admin` can request `audit:read:tenant:*` but must have MFA + justification logged. That justification itself should be an audit event.

sarah.j: Nice. UX question: do we expose a preview of redacted event schema in the UI so customers can see what they will get? That helps support triage.

mike.t: Yes — show sample event with placeholders and a link to "request expanded access" which triggers an enterprise workflow.

jena: Ops details: retention. Customer-facing events default 90 days. Encrypted archive 1 year (configurable per contract). Also keep a shorter retention for high-sensitivity fields unless requested.

rafael: Implementation plan:
- Add sensitivity flag and archived_encrypted_blob to schema
- In ingestion pipeline, tag sensitivity using rules engine
- Implement redaction filter for projection service
- Add token introspection + field-level claims
- UI: sample projection and request workflow

priya.k: Risk: if we rely on runtime tagging, a bug can under-tag and leak PII. Mitigate: build static analyzers and a CI check that runs simulated requests through a sandbox to verify tagging for new code paths.

sarah.j: Agreed — add a mandatory policy: any PR touching authentication/authorization/audit paths must include a tagging test.

mike.t: Ops-bot note: deploy preview for redaction service in test-org-1 scheduled for tomorrow 10:00 PST (:rocket:)

ops-bot: Reminder: deploy preview created: pr-418-redaction-service -> preview-test-org-1. Link: https://deploys.internal/pr-418

jena: Next steps for RFC: I'll draft a short doc with schema changes + API examples. Can we include an example introspection response like:
```
{
 "sub": "token123",
 "scopes": ["audit:read:tenant:org-123"],
 "fields": ["event_id","timestamp","action","resource","actor.role"]
}
```

rafael: That looks good. Also include an example of encrypted archive retrieval flow and key rotation notes.

priya.k: I'll add compliance matrix for HIPAA/GDPR rows and required controls.

sarah.j: Thanks team. If nobody objects I'll mark this RFC as accepted in 48h and start a small pilot on test-org-1. Please drop any blockers here.

mike.t: No blockers from infra side.

jena: No blockers from product side.

rafael: I'll need 2 days to get KMS prototype ready.

priya.k: I have one blocker: need legal sign-off on customer visibility contract language. Pinged legal.

sarah.j: Noted. Thanks — will wait on legal. I'll open the RFC PR shortly and attach the convo.

mike.t: +1 :thumbsup:

jena: :eyes:

ops-bot: Mention archived tests: 3 failing tests in pr-418 related to header propagation. Tagging @mike.t

mike.t: I'll look today.

sarah.j: End of thread — will follow up in RFC PR. Thanks all.
